entry.title: Block-wide Signature Aggregation via SNARKs
entry.summary:
The debate concerning the choice between flat and recursive SNARKs extends into significant concerns over their security foundations. This discourse engages both critics and proponents of recursive SNARKs, focusing particularly on the theoretical aspects that support these cryptographic tools. While some cryptographers express reservations about the foundational robustness of recursive SNARKs, others accept the incorporation of additional heuristics as a plausible trade-off.
A pertinent study in this field, highlighted by [Relativized Succinct Arguments in the ROM Do Not Exist](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/728.pdf), delves into the complexities surrounding the security proofs of standalone SNARKs when applied recursively. The research underscores the inapplicability of a standalone SNARK’s Random Oracle Model (ROM) security proof to its recursive implementations, suggesting that alternative assumptions or models might be necessary to establish security in such contexts. This examination opens up further academic inquiry into how recursive SNARKs can be securely implemented, indicating an ongoing evolution in understanding their potential and limitations.
